ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 71 of 2008 ss56A–56D (beneficial ownership register), as amended by General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Regulations 2011 regs 51–57 (5% beneficial-interest trigger; CoR 44.1 filing within 10 business days of incorporation and of any change); Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 ss20A–21 (CDD), s28 (reporting), as amended in 2017; Protection of Constitutional Democracy Against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004 (POCDATARA); Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013 (POPIA, lawful processing of UBO personal data); Exchange Control Regulations 1961 (SARB FinSurv, non-resident share subscription via an Authorised Dealer without prior SARB approval where funded by inward foreign-currency remittance).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin (certifying against the original passport issued by the competent authority)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (origin country is a 1961 Hague Convention member); otherwise consular legalization at the South African High Commission/Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO and director (utility bill or regulated bank statement, issued within 90 days)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization at the South African High Commission/Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the local incorporation agent and authorized signatory for CIPC filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization at the South African High Commission/Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Signed Memorandum of Incorporation on CIPC Form CoR 14.3 (executed by each incorporator; foreign signatures notarized)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporator(s) and shareholder(s), signature verified by a Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization at the South African High Commission/Embassy

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory adverse-media, PEP, and sanctions screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and direct shareholders before incorporation against: OFAC SDN List; UN Security Council Consolidated List; FIC Targeted Financial Sanctions List under POCDATARA; EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists where EU/UK payment corridors are used; and the FATF high-risk jurisdiction list. Screening is repeated at bank FICA onboarding and annually thereafter; PEP status triggers enhanced due diligence under FIC guidance notes on PEPs and on targeted financial sanctions (2023 edition).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za); Forms CoR 9.1 (name reservation) and CoR 9.2 (registration of a reserved name)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Filings are made in English; the reserved name must be rendered in the Roman (Latin) alphabet; CIPC imposes no statutory transliteration requirement for English names, and names in Afrikaans or other official languages are acceptable if written in Latin script; the name must be unique and not confusingly similar to any existing registered company name or trademark (Companies Act 71 of 2008 s11(2)(a)–(b)).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Building Society / Bankier (requires SARB Prudential Authority approval under the Banks Act 94 of 1990)
Insurer / Assurance / Underwriter (requires FSCA authorization under the Insurance Act 18 of 2017)
Financial Services Provider / FSP / Advice (requires FSCA license under the FAIS Act 37 of 2002)
Trust (requires authorization from the Master of the High Court for trust business)
Co-operative (restricted to entities registered under the Co-operatives Act 14 of 2005)
University / College (requires authorization by the Council on Higher Education)
Municipality / Government / National / State / South African Reserve Bank / SARB (prohibited state-connection wording under s12(3) absent ministerial consent)
Pty / LTD (structural suffix only, not permitted as standalone elements of the approved name)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: CIPC reserves the approved name for 60 days from reservation; a single 60-day extension may be purchased through the CIPC portal before expiry. If the name is rejected (offensive, misleading, state-connected, or confusingly similar to an existing name or mark), the applicant files a revised CoR 9.1 or, if challenging CIPC's determination, files a complaint with the Companies Tribunal under s160 of the Companies Act within 20 business days of rejection; further review lies with the High Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this ISIC 6201 fintech software entity provided that a physical South African address (not a post office box) is registered under s23 of the Companies Act, is accessible during business hours for service of process and CIPC/SARS inspections, and the virtual-office provider supplies official mail reception and forwarding; a post-box-only arrangement is non-compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 12% unannounced physical inspection probability in the first 12 months for this low-risk software company; probability rises to approximately 45% if SARS compliance filings are irregular, B-BBEE verification anomalies arise, or payment-rail activity triggers bank or FIC suspicious-transaction reporting.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008 (South Africa), ss 13(1), 19(1), 66, 67, and regulations under sections 6-14 of the Companies Regulations, 2011
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) through the CIPC e-Services portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: South African Companies Act imposes no minimum paid-up capital or escrow requirement; shares may be issued at par or for such consideration as the board determines. The Memorandum may authorise any number of shares; no initial contribution is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) the allotment and issue of the initial ordinary shares to the Subscribers be and is hereby approved, each share payable in such consideration as the Board determines; (2) the registered office of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [Address], Gauteng, South Africa; (3) [Name] be and is hereby appointed as sole Director of the Company, to hold office in accordance with the Memorandum of Incorporation; (4) [Name] be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary; (5) the Director(s) and Secretary be and are hereby authorised to execute the Notice of Incorporation, lodge all statutory filings, complete SARS and CIPC registrations, and instruct attorneys and bankers to perfect the incorporation. This resolution shall take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name search in the CIPC database, reserve one primary and two alternative company names, and prepare the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) in compliance with the Companies Regulations. Submit the name reservation application electronically with payment.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of passport or ID of each incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is identical, offensive, or confusingly similar, file an alternative name or an amended MOI with CIPC within 20 business days, or lodge a descriptive reservation with supporting rationale.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC Companies Registration Office via e-Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14) together with the signed MOI and initial consents. Pay the prescribed fee using the CIPC secure payment gateway. The CIPC will review and, upon approval, electronically transmit the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as company secretary or auditor (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, use the CIPC 'Raise a Case' portal to correct and re-submit the defective filing; if the company is inadvertently deregistered, apply for reinstatement under section 82 of the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Company Register Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC certificate verification and company secretarial records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the digital Certificate of Incorporation, then establish the statutory company records including the share register, minute book, and registered office registers. Record allotment of shares and director appointments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any entry on the Certificate or MOI is inaccurate, apply to CIPC for rectification under section 80(2) within 10 business days; resubmission may be made without additional fee if the error is attributable to CIPC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, PAYE/UIF and VAT Registration with SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling or local SARS branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax under the Income Tax Act, register for VAT if taxable supplies exceed or are expected to exceed R1 million per annum (or voluntarily), and register for PAYE, UIF, and SDL if employees are engaged. Obtain a Tax Compliance Status (TCS) pin.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SARS registration is rejected or queried, correct the taxpayer details on eFiling and resubmit; any tax assessment disputable may be addressed through a Notice of Objection within 30 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Premises and Fire Safety Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Metropolitan Municipality – Business Licensing and Fire and Emergency Services Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a business premises/trading license under the Business Act 71 of 1991, and arrange an inspection by the Fire and Emergency Services. Obtain a zoning certificate, electrical Certificate of Compliance (CoC), and post the occupational health and safety notice.
required_dossiers: Lease or title deed of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certification is refused, submit a written reconsideration request to the municipality; for zoning non-compliance, apply for consent use or departure; schedule a fire re-inspection after corrective actions, typically within 14 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipality Business Licensing Directorate under the Business Act 71 of 1991 and the Department of Employment and Labour (occupational compliance)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Premises / Trading Licence under the Business Act 71 of 1991 and Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 compliance certificate

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from EIA authorisation – office-based software development and financial analytics operations not listed in Listing Notices 1, 2, or 3 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations; no environmental registration required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source wastewater discharge; stormwater must be routed to municipal sewer free of pollutants; electronic waste (WEEE) must be disposed through registered recyclers; office generator and HVAC emissions must remain below South African National Ambient Air Quality Standards thresholds; noise and lighting emissions must comply with municipal by-laws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Fire and Emergency Services, electrical Certificate of Compliance (CoC), structural load inspection of the leased premises by the building control unit, and occupational clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 including risk assessment, first aid provision, fire extinguisher inspection, and emergency evacuation plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal at https://www.sarsefiling.co.za
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must apply for a Statutory Income Tax Reference Number via SARS eFiling, submitting the company registration certificate, completed IT77/IT14 application, proof of physical address, and, where applicable, a SARS-recognized tax representative appointment. Non-resident entities making taxable supplies must separately apply for VAT vendor registration on Form VAT101 (or VAT703 for foreign electronic services).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a resident (Pty) Ltd is taxed on worldwide income as a separate taxpayer; non-resident entities are taxed only on South African-source income; no tax-exempt zone designation applies to ordinary fintech operations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a check-the-box regime. Available elections include: (i) CFC high-tax exemption election under s9D; (ii) corporate reorganisation rollover elections under s45/s46; (iii) hybrid mismatch ordering/elective carve-outs under s25L and s23H; (iv) group loss-transfer elections under s45; and (v) doubtful-debt deduction elections under s11A.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, administered by SARS
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 actual or expected annual taxable turnover for compulsory registration; R50,000 voluntary registration threshold; separate R1,000,000 threshold for non-resident suppliers of electronic services under s23A.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS does not currently mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping of invoices. VAT vendors must issue and retain authentic electronic invoices that satisfy audit-trail and control requirements. SARS has issued a draft e-invoicing framework and accepts e-invoicing via eFiling/secure data interchange, but there is no API-based live clearance mandate in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under s11(1)(a) for goods physically exported from South Africa by the vendor or on its behalf within 90 days of supply, and under s11(2)(k)/l for services physically rendered outside South Africa to non-residents, including cloud-based financial portfolio tracking and related software-as-a-service, provided documentary proof of export or offshore service delivery is retained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of lading / airway waybill or motor transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank proof of foreign-currency receipt
Commercial invoice and signed contract/purchase order
SARS-issued export certificate or vendor's own export record where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS audits export documentation, physical movement, and the 180-day foreign-currency repatriation requirement. Unsupported zero-rating is reversed with additional VAT, interest, and understatement penalties up to 125% of the shortfall under s223 of the Tax Administration Act; fraudulent export claims attract penalties up to 150%, potential criminal prosecution, and possible deregistration of VAT vendor status.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) – Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand is freely convertible for current-account transactions, including trade settlement, service fees, royalties, dividends, and interest. Capital-account flows remain subject to exchange-control oversight administered by SARB FinSurv. Non-resident direct equity investment may be credited to a domestic ZAR account as foreign direct investment once reported through an authorised dealer; however, outbound loan redemptions, guarantees, share buy-backs, capital repatriations, and upward revaluation of non-resident loan accounts are restricted and require approval. Profit remittance by dividend is permitted from distributable reserves but must comply with dividends tax and SARS tax-clearance protocols, and must not constitute a prohibited loan to shareholders or related parties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export and foreign-earnings proceeds must be received in South Africa within 30 calendar days of the relevant shipment or service-rendering date under the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual. There is no partial conversion quota; the requirement is full repatriation. If an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) is not held, 100% of the proceeds must be converted to ZAR through an authorised dealer immediately on receipt. Any FCA retention must be approved by FinSurv and supported by export documentation (customs SAD500 for goods, valid commercial/service invoices for software and fintech subscription income).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Standard Bank of South Africa Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-low. Offshore digital EMIs are viable only as secondary inbound collection/settlement gateways, not as primary treasury accounts. Any entity accepting deposits or holding customer funds in South Africa requires a licence under the Banks Act 94 of 1990 or an exemption under the National Payment System Act 78 of 1998. An offshore EMI cannot provide a local ZAR clearing account directly; proceeds must be settled onward into a domestic account maintained at a SARB authorised dealer. Legal constraints include SARB National Payment System approval, Payments Association of South Africa clearing rules, and the prohibition on unauthorised deposit-taking. The intended Stripe and Apple IAP rails should be licensed PSP channels feeding a domestic ZAR collection account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South African banks apply FICA-based customer due diligence at onboarding. For a non-resident-owned (Pty) Ltd, at least one director or senior authorised signatory must generally appear physically before the bank, or before a bank-designated attesting officer, to verify identity, signature mandate, and beneficial ownership. Fully remote opening is possible only where the bank operates a digital FICA onboarding platform with biometric liveness checks and documentary verification, and is frequently denied for non-resident-controlled structures. A local physical registered office, independent address verification, and locally-appointed compliance director materially improve the likelihood of approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder chain and opaque beneficial ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full CIPC corporate extract, share register, statutory beneficial ownership register, notarised passports of all natural-person owners, board resolution approving account opening, written confirmation of the ultimate beneficial ownership chain, and an organisational chart signed by directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-wealth concern for inbound FDI share subscription
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution for issuance of shares, signed subscription agreement, origination-bank SWIFT confirmation, bank statements of the shareholder, audited or management accounts of the shareholder, tax residence certificate, sworn affidavit describing wealth accumulation, and profile of the economic sector generating the funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual office or no physical operational footprint in South Africa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid physical lease agreement for the registered office, letter from the physical workspace provider, utility or council bill at the address, SARS income-tax clearance certificate, PAIA/FICA address verification, and appointment of a South African resident director or anti-money-laundering compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border software subscription revenue and recurring royalty payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed SaaS subscriber agreements and partner contracts, sample invoices and payment-reconciliation reports, SARS tax clearance for foreign payments, current transfer-pricing documentation, intellectual-property ownership or licence registration, and projected annual financial statements demonstrating commercial substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital must be routed through a SARB authorised dealer using a SWIFT MT103 wire. The beneficiary field must state the exact legal name of the (Pty) Ltd, the domestic ZAR account number, the receiving bank BIC, and the clear narrative: 'Inward FDI equity subscription — issue of ordinary shares'. The sending bank must be the same institution holding the shareholder‘s account to preserve the audit trail. The authorised dealer will settle the transfer into ZAR and report the transaction under the SARB Balance-of-Payments classification for foreign direct investment equity. Supporting documentation must include the board resolution, share subscription agreement, source-of-funds bank statements, share certificates, CIPC return, and a FinSurv-compliant inward FDI notification where required. Do not split the transfer or use ambiguous purpose narratives such as 'family remittance' or 'consulting fee'.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound treasury settlements for infrastructure, licensing, and partner pay-outs use the local electronic clearing system for ZAR legacy payments and SWIFT MT103 for foreign-currency disbursements. A local ZAR vendor payment proceeds through authenticated online banking with an underlying invoice and SARS tax clearance where a non-resident is paid. For actual foreign-currency settlement, the company submits a SWIFT MT103 instruction to the authorised dealer with the commercial invoice, proof of service delivery, and the correct SARB BOP purpose code. Payment must be made from an approved FCA or by spot purchase of the currency. For physical-goods trade only, an irrevocable documentary letter of credit may be used, stating Incoterms 2020 and matching the underlying shipment documents. Stripe and Apple IAP collections must be settled through licensed payment providers into a domestic ZAR collection account, then reconciled against monthly payout statements for VAT/income-tax and SARB reporting purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward exchange contracts (FECs) executed with an authorised dealer for realised and anticipated underlying trade or service exposures
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing USD/ZAR where settlement must occur in ZAR cash rather than physical delivery
Cross-currency swaps covering principal and interest on documented cross-border debt or investment exposures, subject to prior SARB FinSurv approval and exchange-control reporting

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 71 of 2008, s33) – Form CoR 36.1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 business days after anniversary of incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of ZAR 1,250 per annum; failure to file for 1 year triggers deregistration and strike-off procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) – Filing if triggered by Public Interest Score (PIS) threshold or shareholder mandate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial year-end; must be filed with Annual Return if required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty of up to ZAR 500 per day for non-compliance; possible compliance notice and/or fine up to ZAR 1 million.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation – included within Annual Return and on continuous basis upon change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with Annual Return; no separate annual filing – updates required within 7 days of any change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative non-compliance penalty up to ZAR 250,000; directors may be held personally liable for inaccurate filings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit mandatory if Public Interest Score (PIS) >= 350. PIS 100–349 requires independent review unless a foreign shareholder holds >=10% voting rights, company is publicly regulated, or shareholder resolution requires a full audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (full) or IFRS for SMEs permitted for non-public interest entities; companies typically adopt IFRS in line with CIPC notice.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All companies must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register and file an Annual Register with CIPC on each Annual Return. Any shareholding transfer or UBO change must be recorded and filed within 7 days, not only annually.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Beneficial Ownership Register (as per Companies Amendment Act 2023)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 2,000 - 8,000 USD for a small technology entity, if audit required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for fintech software companies. Preferential deductions include s11D research and development allowance (up to 150% of qualifying R&D expenditure), s12H learnership allowances, and accelerated depreciation for software and related capital assets. Assessed losses may be carried forward indefinitely.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 (Company Income Tax Return) filed through the SARS eFiling portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months after the financial year-end, or such extended date as SARS may approve. Provisional taxpayers must additionally submit provisional tax returns at the six-month mark and at year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company registration particulars and contact details, including tax reference number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable; the resident company files this section. Non-resident shareholders do not complete this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross receipts from trading and all taxable income, including fees from software subscription, cloud services, and investment-tracking licenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident company reports worldwide income in this field. Non-resident shareholders are not required to enter income here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income, such as qualifying local dividends and tax-exempt interest, reduced from gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This field applies to the South African resident company's own exempt income. Non-resident shareholders should not use this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss brought forward from prior years, subject to continuity of trade and ownership requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident company's assessed loss set-off only; non-resident shareholders claim treaty relief separately on dividend distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income calculated after applying assessed losses, then normal tax at 27%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident company tax liability field. Non-resident shareholders may be entitled to reduced dividend withholding tax treaty rates.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs administrative non-compliance penalties under s210 of the Tax Administration Act: ZAR 250 per day for the first 30 days, ZAR 500 per day for days 31–90, ZAR 1,000 per day for days 91–270, and ZAR 5,000 per day thereafter. Understatement penalties may reach 120% of the shortfall for intentional evasion, plus interest at the prescribed rate on unpaid tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder claiming treaty relief must submit a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) and a completed dividend withholding tax declaration (form DTD) to the South African company before the dividend distribution. The company must retain this documentation to apply the reduced treaty rate at source. SARS allows ex-post refund claims in appropriate cases.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties 15%, interest 15%. Treaty rates often range from 0%–10% for royalties and interest (e.g., under the SA–UK DTA, royalties 10%, interest 0% in certain cases). Interest paid on listed debt instruments may be wholly exempt under domestic law.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: ZAR 10 million for Local File per cross-border related-party transaction category (goods, services, intellectual property, financing); Master File required where consolidated group revenue exceeds ZAR 10 billion or total cross-border related-party transactions exceed ZAR 100 million.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not apply formal Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as in the UAE. However, the Income Tax Act, CFC rules, and the common-law substance-over-form doctrine require real commercial activity, decision-making, and operational substance for tax residence, treaty eligibility, and transfer pricing compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting revenue from the ITR14, inflating deductions, altering invoices, or submitting fraudulent financial statements to SARS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under s234 of the Tax Administration Act: fine up to ZAR 2 million, imprisonment up to 10 years, or both. Additionally, an understatement penalty up to 120% of the tax shortfall plus interest on late payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate, assist, or benefit from evasion may be held jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debt under s163, face SARS-imposed travel bans, and be personally prosecuted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating with no employees, no physical office, no independent decision-making or revenue-generating activity, primarily to shelter income or claim treaty advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may recharacterise the entity as lacking substance; deny treaty benefits, impose CFC imputation on beneficial owners, and levy understatement penalties up to 100% of the shortfall plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in establishing a non-substantive structure without reporting it as a reportable arrangement may incur personal penalties under s167 TAA, be prohibited from leaving South Africa, and be subject to clawback claims from unpaid tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting customer funds through Stripe or Apple IAP without implementing FICA-compliant KYC, beneficial ownership verification, or suspicious transaction reporting, despite the lower-risk fintech profile.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, the accountable institution may face a fine up to ZAR 10 million per contravention; repeat non-compliance can lead to licence suspension and criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be fined up to ZAR 10 million or imprisoned for up to 5 years for repeated violations; courts may order personal restitution of profits and issue interdicts preventing asset disposal.
